sources.role: configuration, SDL2 joystick, state, ROM and image implementation (7.2.0)
official upstream distribution and platform identity

paths.path: ~/.atari800.cfg by default; -config selects an exact file. Portable lookup also accepts <executable-directory>/.atari800.cfg when writable.
paths.naming: KEY=VALUE lines. SDL2 controller keys are SDL2_JOY_PORT_<0..3>_MODE/NAME/SLOT, SDL2_JOY_PORT_<n>_USE_HAT/AXES/DIAGONALS/BUTTON_ACTIONS/BUTTON_KEYS and SDL2_JOY_<0|1>_LEFT/RIGHT/UP/DOWN/TRIGGER; -autosave-config is opt-in.

SDL2_JOY_PORT_<n>_MODE: 0 none, 1 keyboard-1, 2 keyboard-2, 3 parallel, 4 host SDL joystick, 5 paddle. NAME/SLOT identify a host joystick by SDL display name and duplicate-name slot. USE_HAT is -1 auto, 0 axes, 1 hat; AXES is the first axis of the pair; DIAGONALS is 0/1/2. BUTTON_ACTIONS and BUTTON_KEYS are comma-separated arrays for up to 15 buttons (action 0 none, 1 UI, 2 Atari key, 3 keyboard).

paths.path: Guest saves are written inside mounted writable ATR/ATX/DCM/XFD/PRO and other emulated media images. SAVED_FILES_DIR only seeds UI file selectors; there is no universal per-game sidecar save directory.
paths.naming: The image retains its own filename; write-back depends on image and protection state.
evidence: source:sio and image backends in src/img_*.c @fe1d2890d9f05fcecb2fd033d09a5c43f534bebf

paths.path: Alt+S or -state uses a user-selected state file; quick-save is <directory-containing-selected-config>/.atari800-quicksave.state (CFG_data_dir).
paths.naming: Gzip-compatible binary streams begin with the ATARI800 header; no fixed extension is required. Quick-save basename is exactly .atari800-quicksave.state.

paths.path: Optional external OS/BASIC/5200 ROMs selected by -osa_rom, -osb_rom, -xlxe_rom, -5200_rom and -basic_rom; packaged Unix defaults are /usr/share/atari800/ATARIOSA.ROM, ATARIOSB.ROM, ATARIXL.ROM, ATARI5200.ROM and ATARIBAS.ROM. Built-in Altirra OS/BASIC/5200 revisions are available.
paths.naming: ATARIOSA.ROM, ATARIOSB.ROM, ATARIXL.ROM, ATARI5200.ROM and ATARIBAS.ROM are documented names. Upstream publishes no canonical checksums for user ROM dumps.

paths.path: No separate cryptographic key file is required by Atari800.
paths.naming: No key filename or checksum is published by upstream.
